family_name: Multi-step Rule Deduction in Fantasy Scenes (b6)

seeds.scene: A wizard's brewing room with 12 cauldrons in a 3x4 grid, each bubbling with a colored potion: 4 cauldrons are red, 4 are blue, 4 are green. Above each cauldron floats a small wooden tag showing one of three rune symbols: triangle, circle, or square. Distribution: red cauldrons have 2 with triangle, 1 with circle, 1 with square; blue cauldrons have 1 triangle, 2 circle, 1 square; green cauldrons have 1 triangle, 1 circle, 2 square. A rule scroll on the wall reads: 'Only RED + TRIANGLE potions cure dragonfire burns.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many cauldrons in this brewery contain potions that cure dragonfire burns according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Read posted rule, then apply two-attribute filter (color × rune) to count matching cauldrons.

seeds.scene: A magic school classroom with 8 students at desks, each with a glowing wand. Above each desk floats a number tile showing the wand's base power (between 1 and 9). The numbers visible are 3, 5, 2, 8, 4, 6, 1, 7. A rule chalkboard reads: 'A spell SUCCEEDS only if the student's wand power is STRICTLY GREATER THAN 4 AND the student wears a red robe.' Robe colors: 4 students wear red robes (corresponding to power tiles 5, 8, 4, 6), the other 4 wear blue robes (3, 2, 1, 7).
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many students in this classroom can cast a successful spell according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Multi-step: read rule (>4 AND red robe), per-student check. Red robes have powers 5,8,4,6. >4: 5,8,6 = 3.

seeds.scene: A stone summoning chamber with 10 elemental sprites floating in a row, each glowing one of four elements: 3 fire (red glow), 3 water (blue glow), 2 earth (brown glow), 2 air (white glow). Each sprite is paired with a colored gem held above its head: 5 gems are red, 3 are blue, 2 are green. A rule plaque reads: 'A sprite is BOUND when its element matches its gem (FIRE-red, WATER-blue, EARTH-green, AIR-white).' Specifically: 2 fire sprites have red gems, 1 fire has blue gem; 2 water sprites have blue gems, 1 water has red gem; 1 earth sprite has green gem, 1 earth has red gem; 0 air sprites have white gem (1 has red, 1 has blue).
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many sprites are BOUND according to the posted matching rule?
seeds.lever: Element-gem matching across 4 element types; per-sprite check; sum over matches: fire-red 2 + water-blue 2 + earth-green 1 + air-white 0 = 5.

seeds.scene: A stone temple floor viewed from above with 9 rune tiles in a 3x3 grid. Each tile shows a symbol (sun, moon, star, or eye) and is either glowing yellow or dim grey. Layout (row by row): [sun-glow, moon-dim, star-glow], [eye-dim, sun-dim, moon-glow], [star-dim, eye-glow, sun-glow]. A rule wall reads: 'A tile is ACTIVE only if it shows a SUN AND is glowing yellow.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many tiles on this floor are ACTIVE according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Rule + grid scan + two-attribute conjunction (sun symbol × glow). Count sun-glow tiles: row1col1, row3col3 = 2.

seeds.scene: An enchantress's display case with 10 necklaces in a row, each holding a colored gem pendant: 4 ruby (red), 3 sapphire (blue), 3 emerald (green). Each necklace also has a number of small charms hanging next to the gem (between 1 and 5 charms). Charm counts (left to right): 2, 4, 1, 3, 5, 2, 3, 4, 1, 5. Gem types (left to right): ruby, ruby, sapphire, emerald, ruby, sapphire, emerald, ruby, sapphire, emerald. A rule scroll reads: 'A necklace is POTENT if its gem is RUBY AND it has AT LEAST 3 charms.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many necklaces are POTENT according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Per-necklace two-attribute check (gem type + charm count threshold). Ruby + ≥3 charms: pos 2(ruby,4✓), pos 5(ruby,5✓), pos 8(ruby,4✓) = 3.

seeds.scene: A monster hunter's identification chart shows 8 monsters in a row, each clearly visible. Each monster has a body color (red or grey) and a horn count (0, 1, 2, or 3). Left to right: red-2horn, grey-1horn, red-3horn, grey-0horn, red-1horn, grey-2horn, red-2horn, grey-3horn. A rule sign reads: 'A monster is CLASSIFIED DANGEROUS if it is RED AND has 2 OR MORE horns.'

seeds.lever: Two-attribute conjunction with threshold; per-monster scan. Red + ≥2 horns: pos 1(red,2✓), pos 3(red,3✓), pos 7(red,2✓) = 3.

seeds.scene: A fortune teller's table with 12 tarot-style cards face-up in two rows of 6. Each card has a background color (gold or silver) and a central symbol (sun, moon, or star). Top row L-to-R: gold-sun, silver-moon, gold-star, silver-sun, gold-moon, silver-star. Bottom row L-to-R: silver-sun, gold-moon, silver-star, gold-sun, silver-moon, gold-star. seeds.scene: A wall chart in an apothecary shows 8 patient figures, each with a body height marker (numbers 4, 6, 5, 7, 3, 8, 5, 6 feet) and a clearly drawn potion bottle next to them showing the potion volume in drops (numbers 2, 3, 5, 4, 1, 6, 3, 2). seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many patients are OVERDOSED according to the posted rule?

seeds.scene: A library shelf with 10 spellbooks standing upright in a row. Each spellbook spine shows: a title era ('Ancient' or 'Modern') and a chapter count number (1-9). Left to right: (Ancient,3), (Modern,7), (Ancient,5), (Modern,2), (Ancient,8), (Modern,4), (Ancient,6), (Modern,9), (Ancient,1), (Modern,5). seeds.lever: Two-attribute filter (era × chapter count threshold). Ancient + >4 chapters: pos 3(Anc,5✓), pos 5(Anc,8✓), pos 7(Anc,6✓) = 3.

seeds.scene: A wizard duel arena chart shows 6 wizards in a row, each with a glowing mana orb above their head displaying a number (current mana): 8, 12, 5, 15, 9, 11. Each wizard holds a spell scroll showing the spell's mana cost: 10, 7, 3, 12, 9, 14. A rule sign reads: 'A wizard CAN CAST their spell if their mana is GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO the spell cost.'

seeds.lever: Per-wizard arithmetic comparison mana ≥ cost. (8,10) no. (12,7) yes. (5,3) yes. (15,12) yes. (9,9) yes. (11,14) no. = 4.

seeds.scene: A magical creature pen with 9 small creatures arranged in a row. Each creature has a body shape (round or spiky) and an aura color (white, black, or grey). Left to right: round-white, spiky-black, round-grey, spiky-white, round-black, spiky-grey, round-white, spiky-black, round-grey. seeds.lever: Two-step: round AND (white OR grey). Round-white (pos 1, pos 7), round-grey (pos 3, pos 9). Round-black (pos 5) excluded. Count = 4.

seeds.scene: An alchemist's lab bench with 5 mixing bowls arranged in a row. Each bowl visibly contains a combination of 2 to 4 ingredients drawn from: dragon scale, phoenix feather, mandrake root, moonstone, unicorn hair. Bowl contents (each clearly identifiable): Bowl 1: dragon scale + phoenix feather + mandrake. Bowl 2: phoenix feather + moonstone. Bowl 3: dragon scale + phoenix feather + unicorn hair + mandrake. seeds.lever: Subset check across 5 bowls: must contain dragon+phoenix+mandrake. Bowls 1, 3, 5 satisfy = 3.

seeds.scene: A magical market with 6 large two-pan balance scales in a row. Each scale has a colored weight stone on each pan. Stone colors map to weights: red=3, blue=5, green=2, yellow=4 (a posted chart shows this). Scale 1: red(left) vs blue(right). Scale 2: blue+green(left) vs yellow+red(right). Scale 3: yellow+yellow(left) vs blue+red(right). Scale 4: green+green+green(left) vs red+green(right). Scale 5: blue(left) vs green+red(right). Scale 6: yellow+blue(left) vs red+red+green(right).
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many of the 6 balance scales are PERFECTLY BALANCED (left pan total weight equals right pan total weight)?
seeds.lever: Weight chart lookup + per-scale arithmetic comparison. Scale1: 3vs5 no. Scale2: 5+2=7 vs 4+3=7 yes. Scale3: 4+4=8 vs 5+3=8 yes. Scale4: 6 vs 5 no. Scale5: 5 vs 2+3=5 yes. Scale6: 4+5=9 vs 3+3+2=8 no. = 3.

seeds.scene: A massive stone door panel embedded with 12 glowing runes in a 3x4 grid. Each rune is one of three colors: red, blue, green. Distribution by row: row 1 (4 runes) = red, blue, red, green; row 2 = blue, blue, green, red; row 3 = green, red, blue, blue. seeds.scene: A summoning circle viewed from above with 8 candles placed around the perimeter, each candle either LIT (with flame) or UNLIT (no flame). Each candle is on a colored tile (red or blue). seeds.scene: A test arena with 5 wizards in a row, each holding two wands (left wand and right wand). Each wand is one of three core types: phoenix, dragon, unicorn. Left to right wizards' (left, right) wands: (phoenix, dragon), (dragon, dragon), (phoenix, unicorn), (unicorn, phoenix), (dragon, unicorn). seeds.scene: A diagram pinned to a wall shows 6 magical creatures in two rows. Top row (predators, left-to-right): wyvern, basilisk, hydra. Bottom row (prey, left-to-right): griffin, kobold, sprite. Arrows are drawn from predator to prey: wyvern→griffin, wyvern→sprite, basilisk→kobold, basilisk→sprite, hydra→griffin, hydra→kobold. seeds.lever: Diagram-graph reading: count out-edges per predator AND check specific edge to griffin. Wyvern: 2 prey including griffin ✓. Basilisk: 2 prey but NO griffin. Hydra: 2 prey including griffin ✓. = 2.

seeds.scene: A magic chamber with 6 elemental orbs in a row, each labeled with an element symbol (F=fire, W=water, E=earth, A=air). Sequence left to right: F, W, F, A, W, E. Between each adjacent pair an arrow connects them, which shows a small reaction icon: a SPARK (active) or BLANK (inert). seeds.scene: A battle scene shows 5 wizards in a row, each casting two spells simultaneously (left hand and right hand). Each spell has a power number visible as floating glyphs (1-9). Wizard 1: left 4, right 6. Wizard 2: left 3, right 3. Wizard 3: left 7, right 8. Wizard 4: left 2, right 5. Wizard 5: left 6, right 7. A rule plaque reads: 'A wizard creates a CRITICAL COMBO if the SUM of his two spell powers is STRICTLY GREATER than 10 AND the two powers are DIFFERENT (not equal).'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many wizards create a CRITICAL COMBO according to the posted rule?

seeds.scene: A monster lineup shows 8 monsters in a row, each one of three body colors (red, green, blue). Sequence L-to-R: red, red, red, blue, blue, green, red, blue. A rule scroll reads: 'A monster is part of a CHAIN if it shares its color with BOTH its immediate left AND right neighbors. (End monsters cannot be in a chain — they only have one neighbor.)'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many monsters are part of a CHAIN according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Spatial 1D adjacency. Pos 2 (red) has neighbors red, red ✓. All others fail. = 1.

seeds.scene: A labyrinth chamber wall has 10 doors in a row. Each door is OPEN or CLOSED, and each has a colored gem above it (red, blue, or yellow). L-to-R: open-red, closed-blue, open-yellow, open-red, closed-red, open-blue, closed-yellow, open-yellow, closed-red, open-blue. A rule plaque reads: 'A door is SAFE PASSAGE if it is OPEN AND its gem is NOT RED.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many doors are SAFE PASSAGE according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Two-attr filter (open AND not red). Open doors: 1(red✗),3(yellow✓),4(red✗),6(blue✓),8(yellow✓),10(blue✓) = 4.

seeds.scene: A training arena shows 7 wooden practice dummies in a row, each clearly labeled with: armor type (leather, chain, plate) and a HP number (1-10). L-to-R: leather-3, chain-7, plate-2, leather-9, chain-5, plate-8, leather-4. A rule sign reads: 'A FIREBOLT spell is EFFECTIVE on a dummy if its armor is LEATHER OR CHAIN AND its HP is STRICTLY GREATER than 4.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, on how many dummies would FIREBOLT be EFFECTIVE according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: (leather or chain) AND HP>4. Per dummy: (leather,3)✗HP, (chain,7)✓, (plate,2)✗armor, (leather,9)✓, (chain,5)✓, (plate,8)✗armor, (leather,4)✗HP. = 3.

seeds.scene: A wizard judgement court with 8 wizards seated in a single row in front of a banner. Each wizard has three visible attributes: hat color (red, blue, or green), beard length (short or long), and a staff held in hand (visible) — present or absent. L-to-R: red-long-staff, blue-short-staff, red-short-no-staff, green-long-no-staff, red-long-no-staff, blue-long-staff, green-short-staff, red-short-staff. A rule scroll reads: 'A wizard PASSES JUDGEMENT only if ALL THREE of these conditions hold: hat is RED, beard is LONG, AND staff is PRESENT.'
seeds.question: Based strictly on what is visible in the image, how many wizards PASS JUDGEMENT according to the posted rule?
seeds.lever: Three-attribute conjunction. Per wizard: pos1(red,long,staff)✓, pos2(blue,short,staff)✗, pos3(red,short,no)✗, pos4(green,long,no)✗, pos5(red,long,no)✗, pos6(blue,long,staff)✗, pos7(green,short,staff)✗, pos8(red,short,staff)✗. = 1.
